title: Entry into Paradise by merely reciting the kalimah
question: Zayd says: although Muslims openly commit sins in the world and carry out deeds of transgression and immorality; such people pray only a few of the prayers and keep only a few of the fasts of Ramadan; they listen to sermons and admonition and yet remain heedless of the rights owed to Allah's servants; they do not discharge even the rights of inheritance, and they disregard the command of Allah and His Messenger — will such people, then, if at the time of death they recite the kalimah, or the kalimah is granted to them, go straight into Paradise at once without punishment? For Zayd says that by receiving the kalimah every sin is forgiven and a person enters Paradise immediately. Kindly explain.
answer:
Zayd's saying this as a universal rule is not correct; otherwise the denial of countless texts will follow.

However, as for the person who has come to faith and after coming to faith has committed no sin — concerning him Zayd's statement is correct.

In the Qur'an Pāk it is: ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْراً يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ — that is, whoever does good equal to an atom's weight will see it, and whoever does evil equal to an atom's weight will see it.

If a person has committed sins in the life of this world, and the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants stand as obligations upon him, then merely reciting the kalimah ṭayyibah at the time of dying does not bring those rights to an end. Zayd must repent of this statement of his, because this statement of his is against the Qur'an Pāk, the Ḥadīth Sharīf and the consensus of the ummah.

For the rest, this much is certainly established: that whoever recited the kalimah ṭayyibah at the final moment — that is, whose end came upon faith — for him there is the promise of Paradise, and he will certainly go to Paradise.

But that every person goes into Paradise at once and without reckoning is neither promised nor established anywhere. Rather, some people will go into Paradise without reckoning; some will go after their punishment has been carried out in full; some will go by means of intercession; some will be brought out of Hell by the permission of the Prophet ﷺ; and some Allah Ta'ālā will bring out Himself. Some will be taken out of Hell in such a state that they have been burnt and turned entirely black like charcoal. And all of these will be those whose end came upon faith.

All of this is mentioned in Bukhārī Sharīf and in many other books of Ḥadīth.
references: Mishkāt al-Maṣābīḥ, p. 140, Bāb mā yuqāl ʿind man ḥaḍarahu al-mawt
Sunan Abī Dāwūd 2/443, Kitāb al-Janāʾiz, Bāb fī al-talqīn
